examples.en: When is this shop usually closed?

examples.ko: 이번 달 휴무일은 달력에 따로 표시해 두었어요.
examples.en: I marked this month's days off separately on the calendar.

examples.ko: 매주 월요일이 휴무일이라서 미리 전화해 봤어요.
examples.en: Mondays are the weekly day off, so I called ahead.

examples.ko: 도서관 휴무일에는 책을 반납할 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't return books on the library's closed days.

examples.ko: 공휴일이 휴무일과 겹쳐서 하루 더 쉬어요.
examples.en: The public holiday overlaps with the closed day, so we get one more day off.

examples.ko: 휴무일을 확인하지 않고 갔다가 그냥 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: I went without checking the closed day and just came back.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '쉬는 날'이라고 하고, '휴무일'은 가게·병원·도서관의 안내문에서 자주 보여요. '정기 휴무일'처럼 정해진 날을 말할 때도 많이 써요. 반대로 문을 여는 날은 '영업일'이라고 해요.
explain_en: In everyday talk people say '쉬는 날', while '휴무일' often appears on notices for shops, clinics and libraries. It is also used in '정기 휴무일' (regular closing day). The opposite, a day when a place is open, is '영업일'.

examples.en: This park is a good place to rest for office workers.

examples.ko: 집 근처에 조용한 휴식처가 생겨서 좋아요.
examples.en: I'm glad a quiet place to relax opened near my house.

examples.ko: 등산로 중간에 있는 휴식처에서 잠깐 쉬었어요.
examples.en: I rested for a while at the rest spot midway along the trail.

examples.ko: 저에게 카페는 바쁜 하루의 휴식처 같은 곳이에요.
examples.en: For me, a café is like a refuge in a busy day.

examples.ko: 아이들에게 편안한 휴식처를 만들어 주고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to make a comfortable resting place for the kids.

examples.ko: 여행이 끝나면 집이 가장 좋은 휴식처라는 생각이 들어요.
examples.en: After a trip, I feel that home is the best place to rest.

explain: 고속도로에서 쉬어 가는 곳은 '휴게소'라고 하고, '휴식처'는 쉴 수 있는 장소를 더 넓게 말해요. '마음의 휴식처'처럼 마음이 편해지는 사람이나 장소를 비유할 때도 자주 써요.
explain_en: A highway stop is called '휴게소', while '휴식처' refers more broadly to any place where you can rest. It is also used figuratively, as in '마음의 휴식처' (a place of mental refuge).

examples.en: I went to a recreational forest with my family on the weekend.

examples.ko: 이 휴양림은 숲속 통나무집에서 잘 수 있어요.
examples.en: At this forest retreat, you can stay in a log cabin in the woods.
I took a walk every morning in the forest retreat.
I bought a ticket at the entrance of the forest retreat.
I searched for a nearby forest retreat and looked for a place to stay.

examples.ko: 휴양림의 공기가 정말 맑아서 기분이 좋아요.
examples.en: The air in the forest retreat is really clean, so I feel great.

explain: '자연휴양림'이라는 이름으로 많이 불러요. 산책만 하는 공원과 달리, 숲에서 머물며 쉬는 곳이라는 느낌이 강해요. 여행 계획이나 주말 나들이 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is often called '자연휴양림'. Unlike a park for just walking, it suggests a forest where you stay and relax. You often hear it when people talk about trips and weekend outings.

examples.en: There are many military units near the ceasefire line.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 휴전선 부근 상황을 자세히 전했어요.
examples.en: The news reported in detail on the situation near the ceasefire line.

examples.ko: 휴전선을 따라 철책이 길게 이어져 있어요.
examples.en: A long fence runs along the ceasefire line.

examples.ko: 학교에서 휴전선 일대로 안보 견학을 다녀왔어요.
examples.en: We went on a security field trip to the ceasefire line area from school.
If you climb up the observatory, you can see beyond the ceasefire line.
They say my grandfather's hometown is just north of the ceasefire line.

explain: '휴전선'은 선을 가리키고, '비무장지대(DMZ)'는 그 선 양쪽에 있는 지역을 말해요. 뉴스나 역사 수업, 안보 관련 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '휴전선' refers to the line itself, while '비무장지대' (DMZ) is the zone on both sides of it. It often appears in news, history classes and talk about security.

en: find fault with; speak ill of; badmouth

examples.en: It's not good to badmouth a friend.

examples.ko: 친구가 없을 때 뒤에서 흉보지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't speak ill of your friend behind their back.
My older sister criticized the food I made.

examples.ko: 사람들이 제 옷차림을 흉볼까 봐 걱정돼요.
examples.en: I'm worried people might make fun of how I'm dressed.

examples.ko: 회사 사람들 흉보다가 그 사람이 들어와서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled when that person walked in while we were badmouthing coworkers.
I'm sorry I badmouthed my friend without meaning to.

explain: '흉을 보다'처럼 띄어 쓸 수도 있어요. '험담하다'는 조금 딱딱한 말이고, 일상에서는 '흉보다'를 많이 써요. 보통 그 사람이 없는 곳에서 하는 말이라 '흉보지 마세요'처럼 충고할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: You can also write it with a space, as '흉을 보다'. '험담하다' sounds a bit stiff, so in daily talk '흉보다' is common. It usually means talking about someone who isn't there, so it often appears in advice like '흉보지 마세요'.

examples.ko: 할머니는 베란다 흔들의자에 앉아 책을 읽어요.
examples.en: Grandma sits in the rocking chair on the balcony and reads.
Grandma put the baby to sleep in the rocking chair.
I want to put a rocking chair in the living room.
This rocking chair rocks slowly back and forth.
I can hear the rocking chair creaking in the room.
My father takes a nap in the rocking chair.

explain: 사전에 한 단어로 실려 있어서 '흔들 의자'가 아니라 붙여 써요. 베란다나 거실에 두고 편하게 쉬는 의자라서 여유, 휴식과 함께 이야기할 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It is listed in the dictionary as one word, so you write it without a space. People picture it on a balcony or in a living room for relaxing, so it often comes up when talking about rest and leisure.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 인터뷰 요청에 흔쾌히 응했어요.
examples.en: The actor readily agreed to the interview request.
When I asked, my senior gladly said yes.

examples.ko: 아버지께서 여행을 흔쾌히 허락해 주셔서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised that my father gladly allowed the trip.
I felt relieved hearing the cheerful, willing answer.

examples.ko: 친구가 이사를 도와 달라는 말에 흔쾌히 그러자고 했어요.
examples.en: My friend gladly said yes when I asked for help moving.

examples.ko: 그는 모든 비용을 흔쾌하게 내겠다고 했어요.
examples.en: He said he would gladly pay all the costs.

explain: 주로 '흔쾌히'로 쓰고, '응하다·승낙하다·허락하다' 같은 말과 잘 어울려요. 상대의 부탁이나 제안을 망설임 없이 기쁘게 받아들이는 태도를 말해요. 비슷한 '기꺼이'는 일상에서 더 편하게 쓰고, 반대 느낌은 '마지못해'예요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '흔쾌히' and pairs well with verbs like 응하다, 승낙하다 and 허락하다. It describes accepting a request or offer willingly, without hesitation. '기꺼이' is a similar and more casual word, and the opposite feel is '마지못해' (reluctantly).

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 강물이 둑 위로 흘러넘쳤어요.
examples.en: It rained a lot, so the river overflowed the bank.
I poured too much water into the cup and it's overflowing.

examples.ko: 욕조 물이 흘러넘치기 전에 수도를 잠그세요.
examples.en: Turn off the tap before the bathtub overflows.

examples.ko: 그 사진 속 가족은 행복이 흘러넘치는 모습이었어요.
examples.en: The family in that photo looked overflowing with happiness.
The market is brimming with people and energy.

examples.ko: 냄비의 국이 흘러넘칠 것 같으니 불을 줄여 주세요.
examples.en: The soup looks like it will boil over, so please turn down the heat.

explain: '넘치다'보다 액체가 흘러서 밖으로 나가는 모습이 더 잘 그려져요. 물뿐 아니라 '행복이 흘러넘치다', '활기가 흘러넘치다'처럼 감정이나 분위기가 가득할 때도 써요.
explain_en: Compared with '넘치다', it paints a clearer picture of liquid flowing out over the edge. It is used not only for water but also for feelings and atmosphere, as in '행복이 흘러넘치다' (overflowing with happiness).

examples.en: Trash floated down with the river from upstream.
Gentle music is drifting in from somewhere.
The stream is flowing toward the village.
Clouds are slowly drifting in from far away.

examples.ko: 바람을 타고 꽃향기가 흘러와서 기분이 좋았어요.
examples.en: The scent of flowers drifted in on the wind and I felt good.

examples.ko: 강을 따라 흘러온 모래가 바닷가에 쌓였어요.
examples.en: Sand that flowed down the river piled up on the beach.

explain: 말하는 사람 쪽으로 다가올 때 써요. 멀어지는 쪽은 '흘러가다'예요. 물뿐 아니라 음악, 냄새, 구름처럼 천천히 퍼져서 오는 것에도 써요.
explain_en: Use it when something moves toward the speaker. Moving away is '흘러가다'. It applies not only to water but also to music, smells and clouds that spread and arrive slowly.

en: let flow; let pass; let go

examples.ko: 단수가 끝난 뒤에는 처음 나오는 물을 조금 흘려보내고 사용하세요.
examples.en: After the water outage ends, let the first water run for a bit before using it.

examples.ko: 그 일은 웃어넘기고 그냥 흘려보내기로 했어요.
examples.en: I decided to laugh it off and just let it go.
Leave bad memories to time and let them go.
Don't let the day slip by with pointless worry.
They released water downstream from the dam.

examples.ko: 친구의 말을 그냥 흘려보내서 나중에 후회했어요.
examples.en: I just let my friend's words pass by, and I regretted it later.

explain: 물을 일부러 내보낼 때도 쓰고, 시간이나 말, 기억을 붙잡지 않고 지나가게 둘 때도 써요. '시간을 흘려보내다'는 시간을 헛되이 쓴다는 느낌이 있고, '말을 흘려보내다'는 귀담아듣지 않았다는 뜻이에요. 같은 느낌의 '흘려듣다'와 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It is used for deliberately letting water run out, and also for letting time, words or memories pass without holding on. '시간을 흘려보내다' feels like wasting time, and '말을 흘려보내다' means not listening closely. It is good to learn it together with the similar '흘려듣다'.

en: pile of earth; heap of soil

examples.en: A heap of earth from the landslide blocked the road.

examples.ko: 공사장 한쪽에 흙더미를 높이 쌓아 두었어요.
examples.en: They piled the soil high on one side of the construction site.
A car was buried under the heap of earth in the landslide.
The kids are playing happily on top of the pile of dirt.
They are moving the pile of soil with an excavator.
A rain-soaked pile of earth collapses easily.

explain: 흙이 쌓여 있는 전체 모양을 말해서 공사장이나 사고 뉴스에 자주 나와요. 흙이 한 덩어리로 뭉친 것은 '흙덩이'라고 해서 달라요.
explain_en: It describes soil piled up as a whole, so it often appears in construction sites and accident news. A single lump of earth is called '흙덩이', which is different.

examples.ko: 삽으로 땅을 파자 큰 흙덩이가 올라왔어요.
examples.en: When I dug the ground with a shovel, a big clod of earth came up.
The child plays by crumbling a clod of earth with their hands.
Lots of clumps of dirt stuck to the bottom of my shoes.

examples.ko: 나무를 옮길 때는 뿌리째 흙덩이를 함께 파야 해요.
examples.en: When moving a tree, you have to dig up the root ball with the soil.

examples.ko: 화분을 갈 때 단단히 굳은 흙덩이는 풀어 주세요.
examples.en: When repotting, break up any hardened lumps of soil.
The thrown clod of dirt hit the wall and broke apart.

explain: 흙이 한 덩어리로 뭉친 것이라서 '밭의 흙덩이', '신발에 붙은 흙덩이'처럼 작은 단위로 말해요. 흙이 많이 쌓인 것은 '흙더미'라고 해요. '흙덩어리'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It means soil clumped into a single lump, so you use it for small units such as a clod in a field or dirt stuck to a shoe. Soil piled up in large amounts is '흙더미'. It is also said as '흙덩어리'.

en: cloud of dust; trail of dust

examples.en: When the car passed, a hazy cloud of dust rose.

examples.ko: 거리에 흙먼지가 나서 눈을 뜰 수가 없어요.
examples.en: There's so much dust on the street that I can't keep my eyes open.
If you walk past the construction site, you get covered in dust.
The truck sped off, kicking up a cloud of dust.

examples.ko: 비가 오지 않아서 운동장에 흙먼지만 날려요.
examples.en: It hasn't rained, so only dust blows around the schoolyard.
I shook off my dusty shoes at the entrance.

explain: 그냥 '먼지'보다 마른 땅에서 일어나는 흙가루라는 느낌이에요. '흙먼지가 일다·나다·날리다', '흙먼지를 뒤집어쓰다'처럼 짝으로 많이 써요.
explain_en: Compared with plain '먼지', it feels like fine soil powder rising from dry ground. Common pairings are '흙먼지가 일다/나다/날리다' and '흙먼지를 뒤집어쓰다'.

examples.en: The yard has a dirt floor, so it gets muddy when it rains.
The kids sit on the dirt ground and play marbles.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 바닥이 시멘트가 아니라 흙바닥이에요.
examples.en: The floor of this shop is dirt, not cement.
I spread a mat over the dirt ground and sat down.
The dirt surface of the schoolyard is wet from rain and slippery.
Walking barefoot on the dirt ground felt new.

explain: 포장하지 않고 흙 그대로인 바닥을 말해요. 반대 느낌의 말은 '시멘트 바닥', '콘크리트 바닥'이에요. 비슷한 '맨땅'은 풀도 깔개도 없는 땅 자체를 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It means a floor or ground left as bare soil, not paved. The opposite feel is '시멘트 바닥' or '콘크리트 바닥'. The similar '맨땅' is used for the bare ground itself with no grass or covering.

examples.ko: 얼굴이 흙빛이 되어 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: His face turned ashen and he couldn't say anything.
After the long drought, the rice paddy dried to the color of dirt.
His complexion was ashen as he came out of the hospital.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 온 뒤 강물이 흙빛을 띠었어요.
examples.en: After the heavy rain, the river took on a muddy color.

examples.ko: 흙빛 벽돌 건물이 마을 입구에 있어요.
examples.en: There is an earth-colored brick building at the village entrance.

examples.ko: 그의 표정은 흙빛이라서 아주 어두워 보였어요.
examples.en: His expression looked very dark, drained of color.

explain: 흙 같은 갈색 계열의 색을 뜻하지만, 사람의 얼굴이나 안색에 쓰면 놀람, 병, 절망 때문에 어둡고 핏기가 없는 모습을 말해요. 이 쓰임은 뉴스나 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 충격적인 소식에 그의 얼굴이 흙빛이 되었어요.
phrases.en: His face turned ashen at the shocking news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀람, 두려움, 병 때문에 얼굴에 핏기가 없어지고 어두워진 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a face that loses color and turns dark from shock, fear or illness.

explain_en: It names an earthy brownish color, but when used for a person's face or complexion it describes a dark, bloodless look caused by shock, illness or despair. This use appears often in news and stories.

examples.en: I want to build a mud house in the countryside and live there.
That mud house was quite cool even in summer.

examples.ko: 산골에 있는 작은 흙집에서 하룻밤 잤어요.
examples.en: I stayed one night in a small mud house in the mountains.
I went to a mud-house experience village with the kids.

examples.ko: 마을 끝에 낡은 흙집이 한 채 남아 있어요.
examples.en: One old mud house remains at the end of the village.
It's a café with a cozy feel like a mud house.

explain: 흙으로 지은 집을 말해요. 황토로 지은 집은 '황토집'이라고도 하는데, 건강과 자연 이야기를 할 때 자주 나와요. 지붕 재료로 이름 붙인 '초가집'과는 기준이 달라요.
explain_en: It means a house built of earth. A house built of ocher clay is also called '황토집', which often comes up in talk about health and nature. It differs from '초가집', which is named for its thatched roof.

examples.ko: 공사장 옆 웅덩이에 흙탕물이 고여 있어요.
examples.en: Muddy water has collected in the puddle next to the construction site.

examples.ko: 수해 현장에서 자원봉사자들이 하루 종일 흙탕물을 퍼냈어요.
examples.en: At the flood site, volunteers bailed out muddy water all day.
A car went by and splashed muddy water on me.
The valley stream turned into muddy water because of the rainy season.
The kids are playing happily in the muddy water.

examples.ko: 바지에 흙탕물이 튀어서 세탁을 해야 해요.
examples.en: Muddy water splashed on my pants, so I have to wash them.

explain: 비가 온 뒤 길이나 강에서 흔히 보는, 흙이 섞여 흐린 물이에요. '흙탕물이 튀다', '흙탕물이 고이다', '흙탕물로 변하다'처럼 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is cloudy water mixed with soil, commonly seen on roads and in rivers after rain. Common patterns are '흙탕물이 튀다' (muddy water splashes), '흙탕물이 고이다' (muddy water pools) and '흙탕물로 변하다' (turn muddy).

en: being muddy; being covered with dirt

examples.ko: 비가 온 뒤라 길이 흙투성이로 지저분해졌어요.
examples.en: After the rain, the road got dirty and covered with mud.
I came back from playing soccer and my clothes are covered in dirt.
The puppy came back covered in mud.
Please leave muddy shoes outside the entrance.
Grandma's hands were covered in dirt after finishing the field work.

examples.ko: 넘어진 아이의 무릎이 흙투성이라 씻겨 줬어요.
examples.en: The fallen child's knee was caked with dirt, so I washed it.

explain: '~투성이'는 어떤 것이 온통 묻어 있다는 뜻으로 '먼지투성이', '땀투성이', '피투성이'처럼 대체로 지저분하거나 좋지 않은 것에 붙여요. 항상 붙여 쓰고, '흙투성이가 되다'로 많이 말해요.
explain_en: The suffix '~투성이' means covered all over with something, and it is usually attached to unpleasant things, as in '먼지투성이', '땀투성이' and '피투성이'. It is always written without a space, and '흙투성이가 되다' is a common pattern.

examples.ko: 갑자기 이름이 불리자 그가 흠칫 놀랐어요.
examples.en: He flinched when his name was suddenly called.

examples.ko: 뒤에서 누가 어깨를 치자 흠칫 돌아봤어요.
examples.en: When someone tapped my shoulder from behind, I turned around with a start.

examples.ko: 차가운 손이 닿아서 저도 모르게 흠칫했어요.
examples.en: A cold hand touched me and I flinched without meaning to.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 제 질문에 흠칫 말을 멈췄어요.
examples.en: The person suddenly stopped talking at my question.

examples.ko: 문 닫히는 소리에 아이가 흠칫 몸을 떨었어요.
examples.en: The child gave a start at the sound of the door closing.

examples.ko: 동생은 거짓말이 들킬까 봐 흠칫 눈을 피했어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling flinched and looked away, afraid the lie would be found out.

explain: '깜짝 놀라다'보다 몸이 순간적으로 움츠러드는 짧은 반응에 가까워요. '흠칫 놀라다', '흠칫 멈추다', '흠칫 떨다'처럼 쓰고, '흠칫하다'로도 말해요.
explain_en: Compared with '깜짝 놀라다', it is closer to a brief reaction where the body suddenly draws back. It is used as '흠칫 놀라다', '흠칫 멈추다' and '흠칫 떨다', and also as the verb '흠칫하다'.

examples.ko: 이 수건은 물 흡수력이 아주 좋아요.
examples.en: This towel absorbs water really well.
I chose diapers with good absorbency.

examples.ko: 어린아이들은 말을 배우는 흡수력이 정말 좋아요.
examples.en: Young children are really good at absorbing language.

examples.ko: 흡수력이 약한 종이는 물을 잘 못 빨아들여요.
examples.en: Paper with weak absorbency doesn't soak up water well.

examples.ko: 이 키친타월은 흡수력 덕분에 기름도 잘 닦여요.
examples.en: Thanks to its absorbency, this paper towel wipes up oil well too.

examples.ko: 흡수력은 좋지만 빨리 마르지 않는 수건이에요.
examples.en: It's a towel that absorbs well but doesn't dry quickly.

explain: 물, 땀, 기름 같은 것을 빨아들이는 힘을 말해서 수건, 기저귀, 스펀지 이야기에 자주 나와요. 사람이 새로운 것을 받아들이는 속도를 비유로 말할 때도 써요. '흡수력이 좋다·높다·떨어지다'와 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It means the power to soak up water, sweat or oil, so it comes up with towels, diapers and sponges. It can also figuratively describe how fast a person takes in new things. It pairs well with '흡수력이 좋다/높다/떨어지다'.

examples.en: I have a habit of humming songs while showering.
The child walks along humming a cartoon theme song.
My older sister is humming since morning, maybe because she's in a good mood.
I hummed along to a song on the radio while driving.

examples.ko: 그 노래가 머릿속에서 맴돌아서 저도 모르게 흥얼대고 있어요.
examples.en: That song keeps going around in my head, so I'm humming it without realizing.

examples.ko: 아버지는 설거지를 하며 옛날 노래를 흥얼대세요.
examples.en: My father hums old songs while washing the dishes.

explain: 큰 소리로 부르는 게 아니라 혼자 작게, 편하게 따라 부르는 모습이에요. 같은 뜻으로 '흥얼거리다'도 많이 써요. 가사를 다 모르고 곡조만 따라 할 때도 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It describes singing along quietly to yourself in a relaxed way, not loudly. '흥얼거리다' is also commonly used with the same meaning. It fits well when you don't know all the lyrics and just follow the tune.

examples.en: I started the new year with a hopeful heart.
The graduates' voices rang out full of hope.
The future looked so bright that I didn't notice the hardship.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 희망찬 노래를 들으면 힘이 나요.
examples.en: Listening to that singer's hopeful songs gives me strength.
Let's start the new semester full of hope.
After talking about the plans, the future looked full of hope.

explain: '희망적이다'가 앞으로 잘될 것 같다는 판단에 가깝다면, '희망차다'는 마음에 희망이 가득해 의욕이 넘치는 느낌이에요. '희망찬 미래', '희망찬 출발'처럼 '희망찬' 형태로 가장 많이 써요.
explain_en: '희망적이다' is closer to judging that things will likely go well, while '희망차다' feels full of hope and drive. It is most often used in the form '희망찬', as in '희망찬 미래' (a hopeful future) and '희망찬 출발' (a hopeful start).

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 본 소방관들의 희생정신에 크게 감동했어요.
examples.en: I was deeply moved by the firefighters' spirit of sacrifice that I saw on the news.

examples.ko: 어머니의 희생정신 덕분에 우리가 공부할 수 있었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to my mother's selflessness, we were able to study.
This is a moment that calls for a spirit of sacrifice for the team.
A true spirit of sacrifice doesn't develop overnight.
Volunteering is hard to do without a spirit of sacrifice.

examples.ko: 위기 때 그 사람의 희생정신이 빛났어요.
examples.en: His spirit of sacrifice shone during the crisis.

explain: 남을 위해 자기 이익이나 편함을 내놓는 마음을 칭찬하거나 존경할 때 써요. '희생정신이 강하다·투철하다·필요하다'처럼 자주 말하고, 비슷한 '봉사 정신'은 남을 돕는 데 더 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: It is used to praise or respect the mindset of giving up one's own interest or comfort for others. Common patterns are '희생정신이 강하다/투철하다/필요하다'. The similar '봉사 정신' focuses more on helping others.

examples.en: I had an upset stomach, so I ate plain rice porridge.

examples.ko: 아플 때 어머니가 끓여 주신 흰죽이 생각나요.
examples.en: I remember the plain porridge my mother made when I was sick.
We eat plain porridge with soy sauce or kimchi on the side.

examples.ko: 입맛이 없어서 흰죽 한 그릇만 먹었어요.
examples.en: I had no appetite, so I only ate a bowl of plain porridge.

examples.ko: 병원에서 퇴원한 뒤 며칠 동안 흰죽만 먹었어요.
examples.en: After leaving the hospital, I ate only plain porridge for a few days.

examples.ko: 흰죽은 소화가 잘돼서 몸이 안 좋을 때 좋아요.
examples.en: Plain porridge is easy to digest, so it's good when you feel unwell.

explain: 흰쌀로만 쑨 담백한 죽이에요. 호박죽이나 전복죽처럼 재료를 넣은 죽과 달라서, 몸이 안 좋거나 입맛이 없을 때 먹는 음식으로 자주 나와요. 간이 거의 없어서 반찬을 곁들여 먹어요.
explain_en: It is a mild porridge made only from white rice. Unlike porridges with added ingredients, such as pumpkin or abalone porridge, it often appears as food to eat when you feel unwell or have no appetite. It is barely seasoned, so people eat it with side dishes.

examples.en: My younger sibling played a prank and giggled.

examples.ko: 아이가 사탕을 받고 히히 하며 좋아했어요.
examples.en: The child was delighted to get candy and giggled.

examples.ko: 형이 제 얼굴을 보고 히히 웃기 시작했어요.
examples.en: My older brother looked at my face and started giggling.
If you write "hihi" in a text message, it sounds playful.
The baby giggles while being tickled.

examples.ko: 비밀이 있는 듯 히히 웃는 친구가 수상해요.
examples.en: My friend who giggles as if hiding a secret seems suspicious.

explain: '하하'보다 작고 장난스럽게, 또는 속으로 만족스럽게 웃는 느낌이에요. 보통 '히히 웃다'로 쓰고, 문자나 채팅에서 귀엽거나 장난스러운 분위기를 낼 때도 써요.
explain_en: Compared with '하하', it feels like a smaller, more playful laugh, or a quietly pleased one. It is usually used as '히히 웃다' and also in texts and chats to give a cute or playful tone.
